expectations.text: Report references the actual user/password with: block from .github/workflows/main.yml, not a generic description of the action
expectations.evidence: Phase 0 quotes the exact yaml block with user/password.

expectations.text: Report explicitly addresses whether token-based auth still works unchanged at 1.14.1 rather than assuming trusted-publishing/OIDC migration is required
expectations.evidence: Phase 3 point 2/3: traced the action's actual twine-upload.sh entrypoint and re-ran its real bash conditional with pybroker's exact input shape, confirming the API-token branch is taken, not OIDC and not the new fatal branch.

expectations.text: Report explicitly notes this action only executes live on an actual release tag, with no CI dry-run coverage today
expectations.evidence: Phase 3 point 3: 'this is exactly the class of finding that CI is green today cannot surface, since it only fires on a real tag push, which CI for this PR wont trigger.'

expectations.text: Report recommends a concrete verification step (e.g. a TestPyPI dry run) rather than a blanket approve or blanket block
expectations.evidence: No mention of TestPyPI or any live dry-run recommendation anywhere in the report. Phase 6 only lists 'migrate to Trusted Publishing' as an optional follow-up. The report substitutes deterministic source-code tracing for an empirical dry-run recommendation -- arguably a defensible design choice, but it misses this specific expectation and drops a layer of defense-in-depth the baseline run included.

expectations.text: Report is explicit about which claims were verified by reading actual code/config vs inferred from the action's changelog
expectations.evidence: Best example across all 6 runs -- dedicated 'Executed, not just inferred' framing repeated in Phase 4 and the would-be PR comment, distinguishing the twine-upload.sh trace and the real sdist/twine check from changelog-only claims.

eval_feedback.overall: Found the deepest, most valuable single finding of the whole calibration round (password-auth now hard-fails on plain username/password per PyPI's 2FA mandate, verified by tracing the actual runtime script and replaying its logic with real inputs) -- clearly beat the baseline on rigor. But it over-indexed on 'I traced the code so I know it's safe' and dropped the simpler, complementary recommendation (a TestPyPI dry run) that the baseline included. The skill should make clear that source-level tracing and an empirical dry-run recommendation are complementary, not substitutes, especially for anything that only executes live in production.
